question: Can the dealing side publish commitments so that a node which fed the circuit something other than what it was dealt can be named, rather than merely detected?
answer: Yes, and the commitments are already published. qomm_transport.roles.Dealing carries share_commitments --- one per share per value --- so that check_share works for a node and adds_up works for anyone. Those are exactly the commitments this combines. What was missing was opening one combination per party instead of one over all inputs.

construction.before: s = sum_j c_j v_j + m, checked against sum_j c_j C_j + C_m. Proves AN input was substituted. No name.
construction.after: s_p = sum_j c_j x_{p,j} + m_p for each party p, checked against sum_j c_j C_{p,j} + C_{m_p}. A failing p is named, by anyone, from published data.
construction.strictly_stronger: sum_p s_p is the old opening with the old mask, so passing per party passes in aggregate.
construction.soundness: unchanged and applies per party: the coefficients come from the commitments, so a node must choose its error before it can see the coefficient that would cancel it. 2^-40 per party.

field_width.finding: NARROWER, which was not obvious. Party p combines shares, which are value_bits + SLACK_BITS = 71 wide rather than 31, so the combination is wider. But the mask is that party's OWN input and is not dealt across nodes, so it does not pay the share slack plus log2(n) that forced the aggregate check to 164.

no_capacity_limit: Unlike the Reed-Solomon decode in qomm_audit.locate, which caps at T = 2 and refuses at three, this names ANY number of substituting nodes --- each party's check stands alone against that party's own commitments. Tested to all seven. That matters, because the case a decoder gives up on is exactly the case an operator most needs a name for.

predictions.one round, unchanged: holds by construction; the n openings are independent

what_is_done: zk/input_check.py build_per_party / verify_per_party, 26 tests in tests/test_per_party_check.py, and the arm in scripts/run_input_check.py that produced the table above.
what_is_not: The circuit still opens one combination. Emitting n requires gen_qomm to keep the per-party shares rather than summing them immediately, and to deal each mask to one node rather than splitting it. That touches the main input path, which every circuit test depends on, so it is stated rather than half-done. The cost is n openings instead of 1 in the same round --- the check's own traffic goes from 0.0126 MB to about 0.09 MB against 19.37 MB for the quote, under half a percent.
what_it_still_does_not_do: Name and stop are different from name and repair. By the time the opening is checked the circuit has computed on the wrong input. This is rung 4, not rung 5.
